# Historical replay compatibility evidence

These fixtures were generated by running the real archived parser, gameplay
simulation, replay materializer and BRD codec. They are deterministic test plays
captured now against historical code, **not recordings recovered from a user's
past sessions**. No judgment, gauge history, result fingerprint or replay event
was filled in by hand. The inputs press the archived chart's active notes at their
old timestamps and release normal notes 10 ms later or LNs at the old linked tail.

## Provenance and reproduction

The capture application is `68382de1627f321aa8a56c7a961d75b4f7b974b7`, including
its entire `src` tree. Its parser is upstream
`14d7a2353102e7ebe3646fd581e1cad7afabdb66`:

- `bms_parser.hpp`: `ce853b35c45f27b2fde0f3c2264ccdef0f6e01c148b005997837035cdb505c42`
- `bms_parser.cpp`: `ad33611897caa887c3e82dbb8edd6602ae40425647334d257acca0eda6c7433f`

The comparison parser is upstream
`5c3bb2faf5d08aa19cc689273e5b107487bf8a5b` (the explicit buffered source-path
API on top of `bb8658a3d68f06c11b4ce4ff0d6c9b91055f2961`):

- `bms_parser.hpp`: `04e16303be71dbb5e6111346d2f43e8413132132070d8937a0d63115ffb90c8a`
- `bms_parser.cpp`: `3ef896b5debec37a826d9a577b44c801fc77e06dd8e13ef12dcb60f439751a1a`

From the application root:

```sh
python3 tests/capture_historical_replays.py --output /tmp/new-historical-capture
python3 tests/capture_historical_replays.py --check
```

Capture requires a **new** directory, extracts the pinned Git revision into a
temporary directory, verifies both old parser artifact hashes, and compiles
against those archived sources. It never invokes Ninja/CMake or modifies the
working parser. Dependencies come from the checkout's existing headers/submodules
and configured vcpkg installation. Check builds the same harness against current
sources. The native `historical_replay_compatibility_tests` target performs the
same fixture checks without recompiling a scratch executable.

`manifest.json` records the old application/parser identities, capture harness
hash, and SHA-256 of every captured chart, BRD, result JSON and SQLite file. Both
the standalone check and native test verify those immutable hashes. The new
comparison is separately recorded in `expected_comparison.json`; it is never
written by the capture or check commands. Updating a comparison requires reading
the actual report and explaining the changed semantics. Never replace historical
results with newly judged results to make a test pass.

## Stored evidence

- `charts/`: exact authored chart bytes, shared by both parser runs.
- Eleven chart `.brd` files: real archived `BeatorajaReplayCodec::encodeChart`
  output, decoded by the current codec and compared with captured raw input and
  setup. RANDOM seed, PRNG and explicit choices are retained.
- Chart `.json` files: old raw inputs, complete saved-result facts/provenance,
  result fingerprints, legacy event tracks, exact-note identities, ghost score
  progression and keysound scheduling.
- `legacy.sqlite`: real version-2 replay tables at user version 13 created with
  `ReplayLegacyFixture.h`, containing the archived materializer's actual events
  and result summaries. This is a schema-2 projection of the historical judged
  track, not a claim to reproduce every older legacy judging implementation. Rows 1–11 follow the harness case order; rows 12–13 are
  the carried course stages. The legacy course links those final two rows.
  Checks open this database read-only and compare decoded events with captured
  evidence before evaluating them on the new chart.
- `course.brd`, `course_ordinary.json`, `course_fractional_stop.json` and
  `course_stage_evidence.json`: two archived input stages with a one-second rest,
  judged with real gauge/combo/max-combo carry. Stage two finishes at combo 8.
  Stage result JSONs are judging envelopes, not independent persisted chart
  attempts: their carried maximum combo can exceed that stage's note count.

The harness deliberately uses normal lane options, classic LN interpretation,
standard gauge, the archived default LR2 ruleset (descriptor version 4),
deterministic seed 123456 and an unmodified playback rate. The orphan fixture is an engine-level capture; it does not imply that the old
graphical gameplay path could render or finish that malformed chart. This
is a bounded parser-adoption matrix, not exhaustive coverage of all replay
options, skins, courses, encodings or every chart in users' libraries.

## Measured comparison

| Fixture | Exact legacy note lookups | Ghost / keysounds | Modern saved facts / fingerprint | Saved playback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary | 3/3 | Equal / equal | Equal / equal | Ready |
| Fractional measure, BPM and STOP | 5/5 | Equal / equal | Equal / equal | Ready |
| LN channels | 4/4 | Equal / equal | Equal / equal | Ready |
| LNOBJ | 4/4 | Equal / equal | Equal / equal | Ready |
| RANDOM choice 1 | 3/3 | Equal / equal | Equal / equal | Ready |
| RANDOM choice 2 | 1/1 | Equal / equal | Equal / equal | Ready |
| PMS filesystem path | 5/5 | Equal / equal | Equal / equal | Ready |
| PMS buffered source | 3/5 | Equal / **different** | **Different / different** | Rejected |
| Null LN partner | Not admitted | Not scheduled | Old evidence retained | Rejected |
| Detached LN head | 2/2 | Equal / equal | **Different / different** | Rejected |
| Detached LN tail | 2/2 | Equal / equal | **Different / different** | Rejected |
| Course stage 1 / stage 2 | 3/3 / 5/5 | Equal / equal | Equal / equal | Reproduced |

PMS buffered parsing changes key mode 10 to 9 and lanes 9/12 to 5/8 despite
identical chart SHA-256. Its unchanged ghost score progression is not proof of
compatibility: keysounds and fresh judgments disagree. Detached LN comparisons
also demonstrate that successful lane/time lookup and an unchanged keysound
schedule do not prove result equivalence. Their new pair identities follow the
reference graph contract; the historical engine did not retain those identities
in its judging definition. A null partner is rejected with an explicit error,
consistent with the reference's inability to process it successfully.

## Runtime compatibility policy

`ChartReplayConsumer` and `CourseReplayConsumer` require saved-result reproduction
before returning a replay adapter. Result drift, carried-gauge drift and course
aggregate drift reject playback. These shared consumers cover Watch, Retry Same,
G-Battle, practice ghosts and video export. Saved result display and byte-preserving
replay/profile operations keep original evidence. Legacy summaries already remain
history-only; the test asserts that none of their playback actions are enabled.

The low-level materializer still returns judged facts and diagnostic tracks for
investigation. A matched score is additionally insufficient when a replay event
targets a detached LN identity: `ReplayData`'s lane/time-only adapter cannot
represent that identity reliably. Such tracks retain diagnostic data but are
rejected by both saved-replay consumers. The runtime `ReplayData` flag also follows
actual live/realtime event conversion into in-memory practice ghosts; the viewer
shows the diagnostic and shared ghost projection refuses the ambiguous track.
This runtime flag is not written as invented historical provenance. This does **not** reject the chart or
all detached graphs: live judging/rendering follow the supported graph, and a
track with no detached result event remains eligible for the other checks.
A future adapter with explicit note identities can remove this replay limitation
without changing historical evidence.

No parser revision was retroactively invented for unversioned replay schemas.
Matching current result facts means the saved result was reproduced under its
recorded policy. It does not certify arbitrary chart semantics or all audio
behavior. Exact note/ghost/audio equivalence is measured separately for this
fixture corpus. There is no automatic migration of incompatible records.
